post.description:
Deploy generated web application to user's GitHub repository.

Flow:
1. Verify user has authenticated with GitHub
2. Generate deployment project from diagrams (web app or standalone chatbot)
3. Create repository in user's GitHub account
4. Push generated code to repository
5. Return repository URL and deployment links

The user can then deploy to Render with one click.

post.description:
Save a BESSER project to a GitHub repository.

Writes the model files (``buml/diagrams.json``, the B-UML sources and
``.besser/project.json``) in one commit, keeping every other file. The
project file the old sidebar saved (``legacy_file_path``) is removed in the
same commit. When the branch moved past ``base_commit_sha`` the commit is
merged with the newer commits. An empty repository gets its first commit
through the contents API first.

the branch head it was read at.

Load a BESSER project from a specific commit in a GitHub repository.

This allows restoring previous versions of the project.

``pending_branch`` is a save or push that did not land on ``branch``

after it: after a merge, the next commit by date is on the other branch.

The files are written for the repo's real layout (see
``render_blueprint.detect_layout``), so what goes live is exactly the code
in the repo. Once the repo is connected to Render, every code save
redeploys; saves that only change the model do not. Answers 422 with the
reason when the repo holds no app BESSER can deploy.

    userProfileModel: <UserDiagram UML model JSON>
    pageName: str (optional)

Returns the same ``{components, css}`` shape adapted in style and content,
ready to be imported back into the editor as a page variant.

Reads the structure of an SDMX dataflow (a preset provider or an https SDMX 2.1 API) and returns
its B-UML domain model as JSON, in the same shape as ``/csv-to-domain-model``.

Accepts a PNG or JPEG image and an OpenAI API key, uses BESSER's imagetouml feature to transform the image into a BUML class diagram, then converts the BUML to JSON and returns the JSON object.

When `existing_model` is provided (as a stringified diagram JSON of an existing
ClassDiagram), the image is merged into that model — same-name classes are
preserved, new ones are added — and the merged diagram is returned.

get.description:
Server-owned limits the KG editor must respect.

``llmRequestTimeoutSeconds`` is the overall deadline of one KG LLM request;
``maxOrphanClassifyNodes`` is the most node ids one ``/kg/classify-orphans``
request may carry (longer lists are rejected with HTTP 400, so the editor
splits them).

post.description:
Parse an uploaded OWL/RDF ontology into a KnowledgeGraph diagram JSON.

Accepts ``.owl``, ``.ttl``, ``.rdf``, ``.xml``, ``.nt``, ``.n3``. Returns
the JSON shape rendered by the KG editor's Cytoscape canvas (``nodes`` +
``edges``) wrapped in the standard diagram-export envelope.

Serialize a Knowledge Graph diagram as OWL (RDF/XML) or Turtle.

The path parameter ``fmt`` selects the serialization: ``owl`` for RDF/XML,
``ttl`` for Turtle. The optional ``vocab`` field on the body selects which
constraint vocabularies (OWL restrictions vs SHACL shapes vs both) to emit;
defaults to ``both``.

Run the OWL2 + SHACL consistency check on the supplied KG.

Delegates to pyshacl (with OWL2-RL inference) plus a small OWL→SHACL
shim for class-level axioms. Returns a list of issues with severity
``info`` / ``warning`` / ``violation``, the offending node ids, and the
originating constraint shape id (when resolvable). An empty issues list
means the KG is fully conformant. HTTP 429 when too many checks are
already running, 400 when the KG cannot be checked (unloadable shapes,
out of time).

Run the KG → B-UML preflight and return a structured list of issues.

Each issue carries a pre-filled ``recommendedAction`` and
``skipAction``; the frontend renders one row per issue with a
checkbox + 2 buttons.

Transform a Knowledge Graph diagram into a B-UML Class Diagram (TBox).

Optional ``resolutions`` (paired with the ``kgSignature`` from a prior
``/kg/preflight`` response) carry the user's accept/skip choices for each
preflight issue. Without resolutions the KG is converted as it is.

Ask the user's LLM for KG cleanup suggestions.

The JSON body carries the active KG diagram, the user's own key and its
provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral or Nebius), optionally a model, and
optionally a natural-language description of the system the user wants to
build (when omitted the model infers the domain from the KG). The response
is a :class:`KGPreflightReport`-shaped JSON the frontend renders through the
existing accept/skip suggestion UI.

Per-node LLM classification for a batch of orphan node ids.

Mirrors ``/kg/llm-clean`` but takes an explicit ``nodeIds`` list and runs
a focused per-node prompt instead of a full-graph snapshot. The response
has the same ``KGPreflightReport`` shape so the AI tab can render it
through the existing accept/skip UI.

Apply Refine-KG decisions and return the cleaned KG.

Single endpoint serving both tabs of the unified Refine KG modal:

- ``source="static"`` (the default): re-runs the preflight and applies
  each accept/skip decision. Orphan-issue ``skip`` choices are deferred to
  the LLM: their node ids are returned in
  ``pendingOrphanClassification.nodeIds`` so the AI tab can call
  ``/kg/classify-orphans`` next.
- ``source="llm"``: applies the decisions to the round-tripped
  ``llmIssues``.

Returns the cleaned KG diagram so the frontend can replace the active KG,
with its new ``kgSignature`` for the next round-trip.

Ask OpenAI to turn an uploaded knowledge graph into a class diagram (deprecated).

Accepts a ``.ttl``, ``.rdf`` or Neo4j ``.json`` export and an OpenAI API key,
and returns the class diagram :func:`besser.utilities.kg_llm_to_buml.kg_to_buml`
proposes. Deprecated: the editor imports an ontology with
``POST /kg/import-owl`` and converts it, deterministically and without a
key, with ``POST /kg/to-class-diagram``.

Validate diagram by converting to BUML and running metamodel validation.

This is the unified validation endpoint that:
1. Converts JSON to BUML (construction validation)
2. Calls .validate() method on the model for structured metamodel validation
3. For ClassDiagram/ObjectDiagram/UserDiagram: runs OCL constraint checks if conversion succeeded
4. Returns unified validation results with errors, warnings, and OCL results

Deprecated: Use /validate-diagram instead.
This endpoint is kept for backwards compatibility and redirects to the new unified validation.

Stream an LLM-orchestrated code generation run as SSE events.

Emits events in order: ``start`` → zero or more of
``phase`` / ``tool_call`` / ``text`` / ``cost`` / ``model_update``
(mid-run outage-fallback model switch) → optional
``error(COST_CAP|TIMEOUT)`` warning → terminal ``done`` (carrying a
one-time ``downloadUrl``) or terminal ``error``.

The ``api_key`` field in the request body is a ``SecretStr`` and is
never logged, never echoed in events, and never stored. The download
URL returned in the ``done`` event is single-use — the first GET
against ``/spec-driven/download/{runId}`` serves the file; subsequent GETs
return 404.

get.description: Return durable lifecycle metadata without exposing request secrets.

schema.title: Response Get Smart Run Status Besser Api Spec Driven Runs  Run Id  Get

get.description:
Polling transport for the durable event log — the proxy-safe fallback.

A TLS-intercepting corporate proxy buffers the
response body before releasing it, which an SSE stream never finishes
producing: either the headers are held so the fetch never settles, or the
connection is torn down ("Failed to fetch"). REST and the agent WebSocket
are unaffected because both terminate.

So this returns the same events as a *short, terminating* JSON response the
proxy can buffer normally. The durable store assigns sequence numbers before
any subscriber sees a frame, so polling and streaming share one cursor:
pass the last sequence you saw as ``after``.

``events[].data`` is the decoded SSE payload, so a client can feed these to
the same reducer it feeds streamed events. ``hasMore`` says to come straight
back, ``status``/``terminalEvent`` say when to stop.

schema.title: Response Poll Smart Run Events Besser Api Spec Driven Runs  Run Id  Events Json Get

get.description:
Replay events after a sequence, then follow the live producer.

``after`` supports the fetch-based frontend. ``Last-Event-ID`` keeps the
endpoint compatible with native EventSource clients. The larger valid
cursor wins, preventing a stale query value from replaying duplicates.

Expose the server's current spec-driven generation configuration.

The frontend reads this once at app startup (or before rendering
the preview screen) so it can show the real hard caps in tooltips,
clamp its own input fields to the server's limits, and surface
whether tracing/checkpointing are on at this deploy.

Nothing here is a secret — everything exposed is either a public
cap or a feature flag. API keys and run IDs are never returned.

schema.title: Response Smart Gen Config Besser Api Spec Driven Config Get

post.description:
Return the plan spec-driven generate would run, without executing it.

The response lets the UI show a confirmation screen before the user
commits their API key and budget. Preview never calls an LLM — the
classifier is pure heuristics plus the project's model presence —
so no api_key is required and the response is instant.

Returns (simplified)::

    {
      "primary_kind": "class",
      "auxiliary_kinds": ["gui", "agent"],
      "target_generator": "generate_web_app",
      "target_generator_confidence": 0.8,
      "summary": "Generate full-stack web app from Class Diagram; "
                 "also using GUI Model, Agent Model",
      "estimated_turns": 18,
      "estimated_cost_usd": 0.59,
      "estimated_duration_seconds": 195,
      "notes": [...],
      "model_summary": {"primary": "class", "present": [...]},
      "model_change": {"verdict": "large", "gone": 0.54, ...}  # modify only
    }

Errors are mapped by ``handle_endpoint_errors`` (``ValueError`` -> 400).

schema.title: Response Smart Preview Besser Api Spec Driven Preview Post

post.description:
Resume a spec-driven generate run that crashed before completion.

Takes the same ``SmartGenerateRequest`` shape as ``/spec-driven/generate``
— the user re-supplies their API key and the current project, which
we hash and compare against the checkpoint's fingerprint before
accepting the resume. The orchestrator picks up from the last saved
turn; earlier tool calls are not re-executed.

Returns 404 when the run_id has no recoverable workspace (either
never existed, was swept, or completed cleanly — in which case its
checkpoint was intentionally deleted on success).

The run_id path pattern matches hex[32] to keep malformed IDs out
of the filesystem scan performed by ``_locate_run_temp_dir``.

Signal a live spec-driven generation run to stop at its next turn.

Returns ``{"status": "cancelled"}`` if the run was found and
signalled, ``{"status": "not_found"}`` if no live run exists for
that ID (already finished, never existed, or download already
happened).

The user's BYOK budget stops accruing once the orchestrator hits
the next turn boundary (typically within a few seconds). The SSE
stream emits a final ``error(code="CANCELLED")`` event before
closing so the frontend can show a definite "stopped by user"
state instead of waiting for ``done``.

get.description:
Download the output produced by a completed run.

Re-downloadable until the TTL sweep expires the entry
(``LLM_DOWNLOAD_TTL_SECONDS``, default 30 min) — a transient network
failure during the blob fetch must not permanently lose an artifact
the user paid minutes and dollars to produce. Cleanup is owned
entirely by ``SmartRunRegistry.periodic_sweep``; this endpoint no
longer deletes anything.

post.description:
Push a finished spec-driven generation run to a GitHub repository.

Unlike ``/deploy-webapp`` (which regenerates deterministically and
would discard the LLM's customizations), this pushes the *stored*
artifact for ``run_id`` — the exact code the user saw and paid for —
plus the re-importable model source under ``buml/``.

Flow:
  1. Gate on the ``X-GitHub-Session`` header (same helper the other
     GitHub endpoints use — the real token never reaches the client).
  2. Resolve the stored run from ``SMART_RUN_REGISTRY`` (404 when it
     has been swept past its TTL — the user must re-generate).
  3. Copy the stored file tree into a fresh temp dir, skipping build/
     dependency dirs, ``.besser_*`` internals, and any ``.env`` that
     carries a real secret.
  4. Inject ``buml/`` model files + ``buml/diagrams.json``.
  5. Create (default private) or reuse the repo, resolve the branch.
  6. Commit what the run changed relative to the commit it started from:
     files the run never held (build output, ``*.db``, symlinks, secret
     files) stay as they are in the repo.

Import an existing BESSER-created GitHub repo as a modify seed.

The counterpart to ``/spec-driven/push-to-github``: instead of *writing* a
finished run to GitHub, this *reads* a repo we previously created (so
it carries the generated code plus a re-importable ``buml/diagrams.json``)
back into the editor so the user can continue from it.

Flow:
  1. Gate on the ``X-GitHub-Session`` header (same helper the other
     GitHub endpoints use — the real token never reaches the client).
  2. Resolve the target branch (repo default when none is requested).
  3. Pin the branch head, then download + extract the repo at that
     commit into the shared run workspace.
  4. Register that code tree as a run in ``SMART_RUN_REGISTRY`` under a
     fresh ``run_id``. A later ``/spec-driven/generate`` with
     ``mode="modify"`` and ``base_run_id=run_id`` seeds its workspace from
     exactly this tree, in whichever container runs it.
  5. Read ``buml/diagrams.json`` (the re-importable model) if present.

Returns ``{ run_id, project, has_model, owner, repo, branch, commit_sha,
message }``.
``project`` is the parsed ``diagrams.json`` (or ``null`` when the repo
has no BESSER model — the frontend must then tell the user to open the
repo in the editor first before it can be smart-modified).

Accept one study telemetry event.

Always 204 for well-formed input, whether or not the event was
stored — a disabled deployment is indistinguishable from an enabled
one, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe server configuration.
422 only for malformed input (invalid session/participant/kind, or a
payload whose serialized form exceeds the size cap).

get.description:

Requires ``X-Telemetry-Token`` to match ``BESSER_TELEMETRY_ADMIN_TOKEN``.
Answers 404 when no admin token is configured (the endpoint should be
indistinguishable from absent on deployments without telemetry) and 403 for a
missing or wrong token.

ImportGitHubRunRequest.title: ImportGitHubRunRequest
ImportGitHubRunRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /besser_api/spec-driven/import-github-run``.

Points the editor at an existing repo that BESSER created (so it
carries ``buml/diagrams.json`` + the generated code). The endpoint
downloads the repo, registers its code tree as a run — so the returned
``run_id`` can be used as a modify seed (``base_run_id``) — and returns
the repo's re-importable model.

Attributes
----------
owner
    Repository owner (login).
repo
    Repository name.
branch
    Optional branch/ref to import. When omitted the repo default is
    resolved.
demo_token
    The demo-link secret (``?demo=<token>``). When valid, a repo without
    readable data classes is read by the sponsored (demo) model instead
    of the keyless one.
allow_ai_reading
    The user allowed BESSER to send the repo's code to an AI model when it
    cannot read the data classes directly. Without it no model is called;
    the response offers the reading instead (``ai_reading_offered``).

SmartGenerateRequest.title: SmartGenerateRequest
SmartGenerateRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /besser_api/spec-driven/generate``.

Attributes
----------
project
    The full ``ProjectInput`` payload (same shape as the existing
    ``/generate-output-from-project`` endpoint).
instructions
    Natural-language description of what to build. Typically refined
    by the modeling agent before being sent.
api_key
    The user's Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, or Nebius Token Factory API
    key. BYOK — sent only
    in the POST body, never in the URL, never logged, never persisted.
provider
    Which provider the key is for.
llm_model
    Optional model override (e.g. ``claude-sonnet-4-5``, ``gpt-4o``).
max_cost_usd
    Soft cap for LLM spend in USD. Clamped to the server hard cap.
max_runtime_seconds
    Soft cap for total wall-clock runtime. Clamped to the server hard cap.

SmartPreviewRequest.title: SmartPreviewRequest
SmartPreviewRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /besser_api/spec-driven/preview``.

Same shape as ``SmartGenerateRequest`` minus the ``api_key`` —
preview is a pure-local computation (no LLM call) so we don't want
users leaking their API key just to see the pre-flight plan.

SmartPushDeployConfig.title: SmartPushDeployConfig
SmartPushDeployConfig.description:
Deployment target for ``POST /besser_api/spec-driven/push-to-github``.

Mirrors the ``deploy_config`` block the existing ``/deploy-webapp``
endpoint reads from its body, but as a typed model. ``is_private``
